description: Qualified dividends coexisting with a net capital loss (§ 1211(b) loss offset never touches dividends; § 1(h) keeps the preferential rate): single, wages 50,000, qualifiedDividends 1,324, netCapitalLoss 792. Hand-computed (useFormulaMethod for exact cents, TY2025): capital_loss_ordinary_offset = min(792, 3000) = 792 -> gross income = 50,000 + 1,324 - 792 = 50,532 = AGI (no adjustments) -> taxable income = 50,532 - std ded 15,750 = 34,782. ordinary_taxable_income = 34,782 - 1,324 (qualifiedDividends; longTermCapitalGains is 0) = 33,458. Since taxable income (34,782) is under the single zero-rate breakpoint ($48,350), all $1,324 of preferential income lands in the 0% bracket: gain0 = min(48350,34782) - 33458 = 1,324; gain15 = gain20 = 0. Ordinary tax on 33,458 (2025 single brackets 10%/12%): 11,925*10% + (33,458-11,925)*12% = 1,192.50 + 2,583.96 = 3,776.46. No credits/other taxes apply -> net_tax = $3,776.46 = 377,646 cents.
